Subject: Pinecone + Redwood: pilot for vector storage and S3 archive

Hi Vanessa,

Great to meet you at the conference last week — thanks for taking a minute in the hallway. I wanted to follow up with a concise proposal: Pinecone can run a 6-week pilot that demonstrates Redwood inference runtime reading embeddings from Pinecone with a cold-storage S3 layer for long-term archive. The goals would be:
- Validate end-to-end latency for a 1M vector index with 128-d embeddings
- Measure per-query cost at our recommended replication/replicas settings
- Show failover to S3-backed retrieval for older documents

If that aligns, I can share a short SOW and pricing tiers plus an evaluation checklist. Are you available for a 30-min call next week? CCing our solutions lead for scheduling.

Thanks,
Daniel

Subject: RE: Pinecone + Redwood: pilot for vector storage and S3 archive (internal)

Looping in technical notes after reviewing Pinecone pricing and our checklist. High-level risks and asks:

1) Networking/KMS
- We should confirm whether Pinecone needs VPC peering or if a private link is available; S3 will need our KMS policy to avoid cross-account key exposure.

2) Latency profile
- If we keep replication factor at 2 and use nn-descent fallbacks, we expect 95th latency to be ~25ms extra per call; need to validate with a 100k warm and 900k cold mix.

3) Consistency model and cold-storage fallback
- Need clear contract for when Redwood should fall back to S3 (age threshold, miss-rate), and whether Pinecone can expose prefetch hooks.

Attachments: inference-dataflow-diagram.png, slo-benchmarks.txt

Proposed internal acceptance criteria (short):
- 95th latency under production pattern <= 150ms for typical 512-token generation workload
- End-to-end cost per query under $0.004 at our target QPS simulated in pilot
- Failover verified with 10% random cold fetches across dataset

If Pinecone can meet the above and sign a basic PSA, we move to pilot. Otherwise we ask Weaviate for a parallel comparison.

-Marissa
